title: Physics: Electricity & Magnetism
description: Electric fields, circuits, magnetic forces, and induction as foundations for instrumentation, stimulation, sensing, and electrochemical biology.

modifications: Expanded the week-1 electrostatics reading with potential-versus-energy distinctions, uniform-field sign reasoning, conductor equilibrium, parallel-plate capacitance and capacitor energy calculations; clarified both objectives and mapped them to outcome 1.

Expanded the week-5 current and RC reading with current and ohmic-resistance definitions, unit-checked time constants, charging/discharging step responses, and instrument-loading limits; clarified both objectives and mapped them to outcome 2.

Expanded the week-8 magnetic-forces and induction reading with cross-product force direction, magnetic flux, Faraday emf magnitude, Lenz-law direction and circuit limits; clarified objectives and mapped them to outcome 3.

Expanded the week-12 electrode and impedance reading with bounded interface models, resistance-divider loading, differential measurement, and careful interpretation of baseline drift; clarified objectives and mapped them to outcome 4.

Added original two-source electromagnetic-wave interference instruction and formative practice in the existing week-11 wave block. MIT OCW 8.02 Spring 2007 class topics and interference problem-solving note are link-only scope references; antenna radiation generation and diffraction remain outside this bounded addition.

outcomes.description: Use field and potential models for charge distributions.
Relate circuit measurements to sensor loading and safety limits.
Apply the Ampère–Maxwell law and Poynting energy flux to ideal time-varying fields and plane waves.
Analyze coherent electromagnetic-wave interference using path difference, phase and the stated geometric assumptions.

lesson_objectives.description: Interpret potential difference as energy per charge and calculate energy stored by an ideal capacitor.
Relate parallel-plate geometry and electric field to capacitance and stored energy, checking units and assumptions.
Calculate the time constant of a series resistor-capacitor circuit from R and C, using consistent units.
Predict ideal capacitor charging and discharging voltages from an initial value and the circuit time constant.
Calculate induced-emf magnitude from a changing magnetic flux and account for the number of coil turns.
Apply Faraday's and Lenz's laws to relate changing flux to induced-emf magnitude and direction.
Calculate voltage-divider loading from a sensor's source resistance and a measurement input resistance in a stated model.
Explain how electrode-interface potentials and impedance can alter a recorded trace, and qualify what a trace alone can establish.
Calculate a cell's membrane capacitance from specific capacitance and area, and relate it to the dielectric constant and thickness with C = εA/d.
Compute the charge and number of ions needed to change membrane potential and compare it with the ions present in the cell.
Calculate the electric field across the membrane and the membrane RC time constant, and interpret both.
Calculate the magnetic force on a moving charge and the voltage across a conducting fluid flowing through a magnetic field.
Apply Faraday's law to compute the voltage induced in a coil by a changing magnetic field, and use Lenz's law to give its direction.
Use circuit measurements to design a current limit and to estimate a leakage current, relating both to a stated safety limit.
Add vector source fields and scalar potentials with signed charges.
Relate potential gradients to test-charge force and energy.
Check flux and spherical charge-distribution assumptions.
Calculate capacitance, plate charge and stored energy.
Distinguish fixed-charge and fixed-voltage boundary conditions.
Evaluate source-work and mechanical-transfer energy ledgers.
Apply loaded node-current and loop-voltage balances.
Calculate resistive Thevenin equivalents and finite-input attenuation.
Distinguish power, port-model scope and reporting calibration.
Solve an RC transition with a stated initial voltage.
Balance source work, stored energy and resistor loss.
Evaluate time-constant parameter and measurement inference.
Compute signed magnetic forces with consistent axes.
Calculate ideal orbits and selected current-source fields.
Distinguish magnetic deflection, work and symmetry assumptions.
Calculate signed flux linkage and apply a stated Lenz convention.
Compare motional emf and closed-loop current assumptions.
Balance RL state energy and resistive or mechanical power.
Calculate complex input transfer and its frequency limits.
Distinguish peak/RMS and real/reactive power.
Separate source loading, reporting correction and biological inference.
Summarize raw voltage reports and determine reference-based reporting calibration.
Recover source resistance and input capacitance under a declared loading model.
Distinguish reporting, loading dynamics and conditional case inference.
Explain how changing electric flux makes the Ampère–Maxwell circulation consistent across surfaces spanning a charging capacitor.
Calculate the magnetic field of an ideal circular charging capacitor from its enclosed displacement current, with scale and unit checks.
Determine the field relation, direction and peak or average energy flux of an ideal sinusoidal plane wave under stated assumptions.
Relate path difference and phase difference to constructive/destructive interference and the resulting intensity for coherent waves.
Calculate two-source fringe positions and spacing under stated far-field, small-angle assumptions.
Use the Biot–Savart law to find the field of a circular loop on its axis and of a finite straight segment, and compare them with idealized infinite models.
Apply Ampère's law to symmetric current distributions, including inside a thick wire and in a toroid, and calculate the force per length between parallel wires.
Calculate a current loop's magnetic dipole moment, its torque and potential energy in a uniform field, and the far-field approximation, and state when each model fails.
Integrate nonuniform enclosed charge before applying cylindrical symmetry.
Recover a distributed-source potential with a declared finite reference.
Check the induced conductor surface sign and electrostatic boundary.
Compare distributed energy integrals without treating the insulator as one terminal.
Check passive coupling and a mutual-energy cross term.
Verify signed port power against the stored-energy derivative.
Distinguish a valid mutual sign from an inconsistent coefficient table.
Close induced emf, drag and externally supplied mechanical power.
Match a source boundary to two-sided outward electromagnetic power.
Use wavelength and retarded time without treating a remote field as instantaneous source information.
Separate reflected-field boundary conditions from momentum and incident energy flux.
Distinguish standing-field storage from average transport.
Solve a distinct distributed electrostatic boundary problem.
Verify source-energy and conductor-boundary statements independently.
Check a distinct coupled current state and energy rate.
Separate source input, coil storage and resistive loss.
Verify a distinct two-sided radiating source and outward-power ledger.
Compare reflected momentum, standing storage and zero average transport.
Close conserved charge, transient time scale and energy dissipation.
Restrict conservation and energy claims to the mathematical object actually checked.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week undergraduate scope only. Week 1 groups the two related electrostatics readings; week 8 pairs magnetic vectors with field sources and dipoles; week 11 combines original displacement-current, Ampere-Maxwell, ideal plane-wave energy and two-source interference instruction after magnetic induction. The 16 instructional readings and synthetic-data lab use public ungraded practice. Antenna radiation generation and diffraction remain outside this package; the RLC portfolio remains inactive, there are no graded homework sets or exams, and workload is unmeasured. This schedule is not evidence of semester equivalence.

modules.title: Electric fields, potential, and capacitance

lessons.title: Electric fields, potential, and capacitance
lessons.worked_example: A 10 μF capacitor at 3 V stores U=½C(ΔV)²=45 μJ; μF·V² gives μJ. For 2.0×10⁻⁶ F at 10 V, U=1.0×10⁻⁴ J=100 μJ. Potential difference is energy per charge, while stored energy scales with the square of voltage for fixed capacitance.

modules.title: Current, resistance, and RC transients

lessons.title: Current, resistance, and RC transients
lessons.worked_example: For R=1.0 kΩ and C=1.0 μF, τ=1.0 ms. Charging toward 5.0 V from zero, after 2.0 ms (2τ), V꜀=5.0(1−e⁻²)=4.323 V. For a separate R=2 kΩ and C=5 μF, τ=10 ms. Prefixes cancel consistently, and the 63% rule describes the fraction of the full voltage change after one τ, not always 63% of final voltage.

modules.title: Magnetic forces and induction

lessons.title: Magnetic forces and induction
lessons.worked_example: For 50 turns with a flux change of 0.004 Wb per turn in 0.02 s, |ε|=N|ΔΦ|/Δt=10 V. For a second 50-turn coil with 2.0×10⁻³ Wb change in 0.10 s, |ε|=1.0 V. The minus sign specifies Lenz's direction relative to a chosen loop normal; the requested magnitudes use absolute values. A current additionally requires a closed path.

modules.title: Electrodes, impedance, and measurement

lessons.title: Electrodes, impedance, and measurement
lessons.worked_example: For a 1 MΩ source and 9 MΩ input, the resistance-divider fraction is 9/(1+9)=0.90. For equal 1 MΩ resistances it is 0.50; for a 1 MΩ source and 100 MΩ input it is 100/101≈0.9901. These results apply only to the stated resistance-dominated model.

modules.title: The membrane as a capacitor

lessons.title: The cell membrane as a capacitor: charge, ions, fields and the membrane time constant
lessons.worked_example: A 10 μm sphere has 12.6 pF; a 100 mV swing moves 1.26×10⁻¹² C, about 7.8×10⁶ ions, roughly 2×10⁻⁵ of its potassium; the field at 70 mV is 1.4×10⁷ V/m and τ = 10 ms.

modules.title: Induction, flow meters and current limits

lessons.title: Magnetic forces and induction at the bench: flow meters, induced voltages and keeping currents within limits
lessons.worked_example: A 0.1 T field across a 10 mm pipe at 0.3 m/s gives 0.30 mV; a 50-turn, 2 cm² coil in 20 T/s develops 0.20 V; a 10 μA design limit at 5 V needs at least 500 kΩ in series, and 0.35 V across 100 kΩ means 3.5 μA.

modules.title: Superposition, potential and Gauss-law boundaries

lessons.title: Superposition, potential and Gauss-law boundaries
lessons.worked_example: Draw a one-dimensional source map and label the observation point before assigning signs. At the midpoint add two rightward 1800 V/m fields, but add +180 and −180 V scalar potentials. Multiply the resulting field by the independently chosen test charge for force. For the separate uniform sphere, calculate enclosed charge first and use the interior expression only within its radius.

modules.title: Capacitance, dielectrics and energy boundaries

lessons.title: Capacitance, dielectrics and energy boundaries
lessons.worked_example: Calculate vacuum C=17.708 pF from geometry, then initial Q=106.248 pC and U=318.744 pJ at 6 V. For the isolated process hold Q fixed, obtaining V=1.5 and U=79.686 pJ. For the separate fixed-voltage process hold V fixed, obtaining Q=424.992 pC and U=1274.976 pJ. Include source work before interpreting the energy difference.

modules.title: Kirchhoff balances, Thevenin models and source loading

lessons.title: Kirchhoff balances, Thevenin models and source loading
lessons.worked_example: For the 3 V series source, use total resistance 1.2 MΩ to get 2.5 µA, then find load voltage and both resistor powers. For the separate 6 V divider, solve the open-circuit node first and calculate the port resistance after suppressing the ideal source. Add the 100 kΩ load using either KCL or the Thevenin divider and verify both yield 1.2 V.

modules.title: RC switching, initial conditions and energy

lessons.title: RC switching, initial conditions and energy
lessons.worked_example: Start with V₀=1 rather than a default zero state. Use τ=0.10 s and transition amplitude 2 V to evaluate V_C(0.10). Check initial current 10 µA from the resistor drop. Independently calculate initial/final capacitor energies, source charge and source work. Verify 3.00 µJ supplied equals 2.00 µJ stored plus 1.00 µJ dissipated, and compare with a numerical time integral.

modules.title: Magnetic vectors, fields and force-work distinctions

lessons.title: Magnetic vectors, fields and force-work distinctions
lessons.worked_example: Write v and B components first, evaluate v×B and then multiply by the signed charge for −2.4 nN in y. For the independent magnetic-only circular model, use force balance for radius 3.75 mm and ω=800 rad/s, checking unchanged kinetic energy. For the wire segment, use the current-direction length vector. Compare the ideal long-wire and solenoid field calculations only within their different geometrical assumptions.

modules.title: Sources of magnetic fields: Biot–Savart, Ampère's law and magnetic dipoles

lessons.title: Sources of magnetic fields: Biot–Savart, Ampère's law and magnetic dipoles
lessons.worked_example: A 100-turn square coil of side 2.0 cm carrying 0.05 A has μ = 2.0 × 10⁻³ A·m²; in a perpendicular 0.10 T field the torque is 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ N·m and turning it from aligned to anti-aligned takes 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ J. Biot–Savart over four finite sides gives 2.83 μT at the centre of one turn, about 283 μT for all turns.

modules.title: Induction, Lenz signs and inductor energy

lessons.title: Induction, Lenz signs and inductor energy
lessons.worked_example: At t=3, calculate B=0.28 T and each-turn flux 840 µWb, then differentiate the specified field for emf −7.20 mV under the +z/positive-contour convention. For the separate moving bar, find 30 mV and 3 mA, and verify mechanical power equals resistor heat. For the separate RL model, find τ=2 ms, final current 100 mA and stored energy 200 µJ.

modules.title: Displacement current, Ampère–Maxwell law and wave energy

lessons.title: Displacement current, Ampère–Maxwell law and wave energy
lessons.worked_example: For circular plates of radius 40 mm charging at 0.50 mA, the ideal magnetic field at r=20 mm is 1.25 nT and at r=50 mm is 2.00 nT. A vacuum wave with E0=120 V/m has B0=0.400 μT, peak Poynting flux 38.2 W/m² and cycle-average flux 19.1 W/m².

modules.title: Wave superposition and two-source interference

lessons.title: Wave superposition and two-source interference
lessons.worked_example: For λ=600 nm, slit separation d=0.30 mm and screen distance L=2.0 m, adjacent bright fringes are 4.0 mm apart; the third bright fringe is at 12 mm and the first dark fringe at 2.0 mm.

modules.title: Phasors, loading and measurement inference

lessons.title: Phasors, loading and measurement inference
lessons.worked_example: Build parallel input admittance, add the series source drop and solve H=1/(1.1+j). Obtain amplitude and negative phase with the stated convention. Convert the input's peak voltage to RMS before calculating resistor power. Independently factor the transfer into H₀ and τ, then predict how changing only input resistance alters both. Keep reporting baseline/gain correction separate from this circuit transfer.

modules.title: Virtual lab 1: calibration, loading and observed time constants

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: calibration, loading and observed time constants
lessons.worked_example: Independent references identify reporting offset 0.020 V and gain 2. Corrected steady voltages infer 100 kΩ source resistance, and loaded transients infer 1 µF input capacitance. A/B amplitudes 10/11 and 0.5 V have time constants 0.090909 and 0.050 s without changing the source.

modules.title: Series-resonance project guide (optional, ungraded)

lessons.title: Series-resonance project guide: resonant frequency, quality factor, bandwidth, power and stored energy (optional, ungraded)
lessons.worked_example: For a separate series RLC circuit with R = 250 Ω, L = 0.010 H, C = 1.0 µF and V_peak = 8.0 V, ω₀ = 10,000 rad/s (f₀ ≈ 1591.5 Hz), Q = 0.40 with bandwidth 25,000 rad/s and half-power frequencies near 3508 and 28,508 rad/s; at resonance I_peak = 0.032 A gives 0.128 W average resistor power and equal 5.12 µJ stored-energy maxima a quarter-cycle apart; at ω = 50,000 rad/s the +480 Ω net reactance gives |Z| ≈ 541 Ω and a current lagging by ≈ 62.5°.

modules.title: Continuous charge and grounded cylindrical boundaries

lessons.title: Continuous charge and grounded cylindrical boundaries
lessons.worked_example: Cylindrical shells contribute rho0(s/a)²2pi s ds, so enclosed line charge scales as r^4. At half radius the fraction is 1/16. Gauss gives E=K r³/a^4 inside, hence K/(8a)=31.25 V/m. A cross-sectional area fraction would incorrectly treat the density as uniform.

modules.title: Coupled inductors and mechanical power

lessons.title: Coupled inductors and mechanical power
lessons.worked_example: The coupling magnitude is 0.02/sqrt(0.02×0.08)=one half. Energy is one-half L1 i1²+M i1 i2+one-half L2 i2²=0.01−0.04+0.16=0.13 J. The mutual term can be negative while the complete positive definite quadratic form remains nonnegative. Verify the original source, state and boundary equations independently before accepting this selected response.

modules.title: Radiating source, reflection and standing-field energy

lessons.title: Radiating source, reflection and standing-field energy
lessons.worked_example: Tangential continuity and the magnetic jump give electric peak Z0K0/two=0.6pi. Each outgoing side carries Z0K0²/eight=0.0015pi W/m², so total outward flux is 0.003pi. Opposite coordinate Poynting vectors do not cancel energy leaving the source; dot each with its own outward normal.

modules.title: Assignment 1: charge, boundary and energy evidence

lessons.title: Assignment 1: charge, boundary and energy evidence
lessons.worked_example: Enclosed line charge scales as r^4, so E(a/two)=K/(eight a)=20 V/m. Annular integration gives V(a)=eight ln3 and interior integration adds K/four=two volts at the axis. Retain the finite grounded reference, the source distribution and both field regions; the insulating source is not equipotential.

modules.title: Assignment 2: mutual energy and source work

lessons.title: Assignment 2: mutual energy and source work
lessons.worked_example: Self energies are 0.06 and 0.06 J and mutual energy is 0.06 J, totaling 0.18. Matrix multiplication gives voltages 0.03 and 0.21 V. Signed port power is two×0.03+one×0.21=0.27 W, matching the direct stored-energy derivative despite a negative derivative in the first current coordinate.

modules.title: Assignment 3: source, reflection and wave energy

lessons.title: Assignment 3: source, reflection and wave energy
lessons.worked_example: Boundary conditions give peak field Z0K0/two=1.8pi V/m. Each side carries Z0K0²/eight=0.0135pi W/m²; both outward contributions total 0.027pi. The cycle-averaged negative field work on the prescribed current supplies that electromagnetic output, with no finite total antenna-power claim for an infinite sheet.

modules.title: Assignment 4: cumulative boundaries and energy claims

lessons.title: Assignment 4: cumulative boundaries and energy claims
lessons.worked_example: Conserved charge is twelve microcoulombs, so final voltage is two V. Capacitor energy falls from 36 to twelve microjoules, losing 24 through the finite resistance. The voltage-difference capacitance is four/three microfarads, giving tau=eight/three milliseconds, and initial current is three mA. Charge and field-energy statements require separate ledgers.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items to repository maintainers.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added an original lesson on the cell membrane as a capacitor (capacitance, ions per voltage change, transmembrane field and time constant) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added an original lesson on magnetic force, electromagnetic flow measurement, Faraday and Lenz's laws and circuit current limits with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Fixed number formatting that an earlier authoring step left in learner-visible text: raw exponent notation (a number written with the letter e and a power of ten) and floating-point artifacts (a decimal with a long run of trailing digits) in item physics-em-1:capacitor-energy. No answer key, tolerance or objective changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added seven original lessons on field/potential superposition and Gauss boundaries, dielectric energy conditions, Kirchhoff/Thevenin loading, RC state/energy, magnetic vectors/field models, induction/RL energy and phasor measurement inference; one synthetic reporting/loading/transient lab and a proposed weekly schedule. Developed with Codex assistance. Still partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-1 electric-fields, potential and capacitance reading with potential/energy distinctions, field-direction signs, conductor equilibrium, parallel-plate capacitance, capacitor energy and limits of the membrane analogy. Clarified both objectives and linked them and the unchanged practice assessment to outcome 1. Existing question IDs, prompts, answer keys and cards are unchanged. Compact prototype readings remain in weeks 5, 8 and 12; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded week 5 with current and resistance definitions, the operating limits of Ohm’s relation, RC time-constant units, ideal charging/discharging responses, the correct meaning of the one-time-constant fraction and measurement-loading limits. Clarified both objectives and linked them and the unchanged practice assessment to outcome 2. Existing question IDs, prompts, answer keys and cards are unchanged. Compact prototype readings remain in weeks 8 and 12; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded week 8 with Lorentz-force direction and work limits, current-segment force, magnetic flux and orientation, Faraday emf magnitudes, Lenz-law direction, and the distinction between emf and closed-path current. Clarified both objectives and linked them and the unchanged practice assessment to outcome 3. Existing question IDs, prompts, answer keys and cards are unchanged. One compact prototype reading remains in week 12; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded week 12 with a bounded electrode-interface model, resistance-divider loading, differential measurement, and limits on baseline-drift inference. Clarified both objectives and linked them and the unchanged practice assessment to outcome 4. Existing question IDs, prompts, answer keys and cards are unchanged. All 13 readings now have substantive instruction; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an inactive series-resonance portfolio with fictional RLC candidates, half-power bandwidth, peak/RMS current and average-power checks, and an ideal energy comparison. The model is a paper exercise, not a device design; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added original instruction on displacement current, charging-capacitor current continuity, Ampère–Maxwell circulation, magnetic field between circular plates, plane-wave Poynting flux and cycle-average energy flow. MIT OCW 8.02 class topics is a scope comparator only. Grouped two related electrostatics readings in week 1 to fit the new unit into the proposed 14-week sequence. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an original two-source electromagnetic-wave interference reading to the existing week-11 wave block, with six numeric checks, two multiple-select items and four retrieval cards. The unit covers path/phase conditions, equal-source intensity and far-field fringe geometry; antenna radiation generation and diffraction remain deferred. MIT OCW 8.02 Spring 2007 was used as a link-only scope comparator. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Grouped an original magnetic-field-sources reading with the week-8 magnetic-vectors lesson: Biot–Savart fields of a loop on its axis, finite segments and a square loop; Ampère's law inside a thick wire, in a toroid and between parallel wires; and magnetic dipole moment, torque, energy and the axial far field. Added three objectives, eleven formative items and four cards, with no week added. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Made the planned series-resonance project usable by learners as ungraded practice. Week 13 gains an optional project guide with the candidates, brief and six tasks, a worked example on a separate circuit, a rehearsal circuit and six open rehearsal practice items; six project milestones are Case studio self-checks with a week-14 project record. The loading lab's dataset link now points to the package-pinned CSV instead of a mutable repository URL. The inactive project draft is unchanged; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added original continuous-charge/grounded-boundary energy, coupled-inductor/mechanical power and radiating-sheet/reflection/standing-energy foundations; four connected field/induction/wave/cumulative reports and twenty checkpoints/cards. Preserves earlier project, lab and numeric keys. Explicit source/state/boundary, signed-power and distributed-energy distinctions; partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

limitations: Nineteen topic readings and four connected reports accompany one synthetic data lab and the optional project guide; this is not a full university semester.

The proposed 14-week sequence is unmeasured and unreviewed; its opening electrostatics block combines two related readings, and week 8 pairs magnetic vectors with field sources and dipoles. Graded homework, exams and a full laboratory sequence remain absent; the new RLC portfolio is inactive and ungraded.
New worked systems and parameters are synthetic; selected electrostatic, lumped-element and prescribed-field models provide no real apparatus or human-subject procedure.
Public keys and feedback remain formative authoring specifications; practice points are not course grades.
Subject-matter, accessibility and workload review remain outstanding; the original text circuit map has a verbal description but no assistive-technology review.
The initial four OpenStax sections remain link-only references; no teaching text, problem, figure or dataset was imported.
Fourteen primary OpenStax University Physics Volume 2 section pages are registered as link-only references; no prose, problem, figure or dataset was imported.

The series-resonance project is optional and ungraded. Its six milestones are Case studio self-checks whose private drafts are never submitted or scored; the rehearsal practice uses a separate synthetic circuit, and no software check evaluates a learner's derivation or written interpretation. Milestone weeks are planning suggestions, not measured workload or deadlines.

Three selected foundations and four connected open reports deepen continuous nonuniform charge/boundaries/energy, mutual coupling and mechanical induction power, source generation from an ideal infinite sheet, conducting reflection and standing-field storage/transport. Four reports do not reproduce the source course’s TEAL experimental/group format or complete assessment depth. Workload and qualified review remain open.

All new geometries, circuits and waves are prescribed synthetic mathematical models, not tissue fields, finite antenna designs, exposure limits or equipment validation. The infinite sheet has finite power per area, not finite total antenna power. Grounded and isolated boundaries, signed source work and stored/transported energy require separate ledgers. Code, diagrams, derivations, plots and reports are retained locally and ungraded; finite-end/antenna/diffraction, lossy materials and nonlinear cores remain deferred.

Of the 145 numerical answers, 15 require units, 63 check significant figures and 0 check dimensions. New continuous checkpoint quantities request three significant figures; written arguments are not automatically evaluated.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments, a complete laboratory sequence, an active graded project, measured workload and qualified human review remain outstanding.
